text: . Moldova temporarily closed its airspace on Tuesday following a drone incursion, delaying a flight carrying Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to Norway.Government spokesperson Dumitru Ciorici said the airspace was closed to protect aircraft flying over the country, delaying three departures, including Zelenskyy’s flight. The restrictions were later lifted and the plane took off.Moldovan police said a Russian drone crashed in a sunflower field near a village in Riscani district, triggering four fires. No injuries were reported.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. In US Open Tennis, Defending women’s singles champion and top seed Aryna Sabalenka will take on sixth seed Linda Nosková of Czech Republic in quarterfinal tonight. In  another quarterfinal matches of Men’s Singles, 11th seed Frances Tiafoe will be up against the unseeded Alex Michelsen in the all-American fixture tonight.In other Women’s Singles last-eight matches, third seed Jessica Pegula will face 26th seed Emma Navarro in all-American clash tomorrow morning. American sensation and fourth seed Coco Gauff will face fifth seed Mirra Andreeva of Russia tomorrow night. Second seed Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan will lock horns with Qinwen Zheng of China tomorrow.Men’s reigning champion Carlos Alcaraz of Spain will face eighth seed American Ben Shelton tomorrow morning.Top seed German Alexander Zverev will lock horns with Botic van de Zandschulp Netherlands tomorrow night.28th seed Belgian Alexander Blockx will meet unseeded Russian Karen Khachanov tomorrow.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. The country’s automobile retail sales rose 17.51 per cent year on year to over 24 lakh units in August this year, according to a report released by the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations. Sales of alternative-fuel passenger vehicles, including CNG, hybrids and electric vehicles, surpassed petrol-powered vehicles for the first time, accounting for 41.95 per cent of the market. Petrol vehicles held a 40.85 per cent share, marking a significant structural shift in consumer preferences.Passenger vehicle (PV) sales grew 16.14 per cent, while commercial vehicle (CV) sales increased 14.45 per cent year on year in August. Rural automobile sales also outperformed their urban counterparts, growing 19.79 per cent annually compared with 15.17 per cent growth in urban sales.

. Prince Rahim Aga Khan V, the 50th hereditary Imam of the Ismaili Muslim Community and Chair of the Aga Khan Development Network, has arrived in New Delhi on his maiden visit to India. He was welcomed by an Indian delegation on his arrival.The Ministry of External Affairs extended a warm welcome to Prince Rahim Aga Khan V, saying that the visit will provide an opportunity to review ongoing cooperation with the Aga Khan Development Network in social development and heritage preservation and explore collaboration on development and community initiatives.Prince Rahim Aga Khan is visiting India until the 15th of this month at the invitation of Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan. He will hold talks with the Vice President today. During his stay in New Delhi, the Aga Khan will also call on President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He will also meet Home Minister Amit Shah and External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar.The External Affairs Ministry said, as part of the visit, the dignitary is also slated to travel to Ahmedabad, Mumbai, and Hyderabad, where the Aga Khan Development Network is involved in various development and community initiatives. This is the first visit of Prince Rahim Aga Khan V to India since his accession as the 50th Imam of the Ismaili community.

. The Ministry of Interior of Thailand has said that Indian tourists holding ordinary passports are exempt from visa requirements and permitted to stay in Thailand not exceeding 30 days. The exemption will be implemented with effect from 15 of this month. The Indian Embassy in Thailand, in a social media post, said visitors must carry a valid passport with at least six months’ validity from the date of arrival. They should also have confirmed return tickets, hotel bookings, and clear travel plans and itineraries. It added that Visitors are required to complete the Thailand Digital Arrival Card within 72 hours before arrival through the official immigration website. The Embassy also advised travellers to obtain appropriate visas if their visit is for purposes not covered under the visa exemption facility. Tourists availing themselves of the visa exemption facility should carry at least 20 thousand Thai Baht in cash per passenger.The Embassy advised travellers to keep all required documents readily available while approaching the Immigration counter on arrival. In case of group travel, each member must carry the required documents individually. Travellers who have received a job offer in Thailand have been advised not to use the visa exemption facility. Those transiting through Thailand should also carry all relevant documents and visas, as required, for their final destination.

. In Badminton, Indian pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty clinched the men’s doubles title at the China Masters in Shenzhen today. The Indian duo defeated China’s He Ji Ting and Ren Xiang Yu 11-21, 21-13, 21-17 in the summit clash to secured India’s first-ever title at the China Masters.The victory marks the duo’s second title of the season. They had earlier won the Singapore Open Super 750 and finished runners-up at the Thailand Open Super 500. Satwik and Chirag booked their place in the final after defeating Malaysia’s Nur Mohd Azriyn Ayub and Tan Wee Kiong 21-15, 18-21, 21-11 in the semifinals. The Indian duo had finished runners-up at the China Masters in 2023 and 2025 and reached the semifinals in 2024.

. The US-Iran conflict has seen sharp escalation since yesterday, with both sides reporting attacks on military infrastructure and commercial shipping vessels. The recent attacks are perhaps the biggest on shipping vessels since the beginning of the conflict. US CENTCOM had said it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday, after Iranian forces attempted to strike a US Navy warship with ballistic missiles. The US identified the 5 Iranian vessels as Kaviz, Charminar, Horizon 1, Riesco and Derya. The US says the warship successfully evaded the Iranian attacks and that no American personnel were injured. Iran has claimed larger attacks by its forces in retaliation. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said they attacked two US naval vessels and eight oil tankers near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran also fired multiple missiles towards US Military Bases in Jordan.While the US CENTCOM has denied the claims of US Navy warships being hit, the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency, or UKMTO has confirmed that several merchant vessels in the Northern Arabian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman were hit by disabling fire during overnight military activity. In a separate incident, another vessel near Port Rashid in the UAE was seen listing (listing refers to a ship tilting on one side due to weight balance) after what UKMTO described as a possible attack by an unknown projectile. UKMTO is a maritime security agency that provides mariners, shipping companies, and regional authorities with verified security information on threats and incidents affecting commercial shipping in the region.A Panama-flagged tanker New Andros, carrying around two million barrels of Iraqi fuel oil, was also reported to be hit by a drone in Iraqi waters. The conflict has also widened into the broader region with Houthi forces recently attacking several facilities in Saudi Arabia.These developments have sent oil prices higher, with Brent crude crossing the 100 USD per barrel mark and WTI moving above 95 USD today, rising by almost 3 percent. Brent is the benchmark used to price a very large share of internationally traded crude. WTI, or West Texas Intermediate, is the main US crude-oil benchmark, representing light, sweet crude produced in the United States. With shipping lanes and energy infrastructure increasingly coming under attack, prolonged disruption could put further upward pressure on oil prices and add to global economic pressures.

. India and Sri Lanka exchanged  Memorandum of Understandings (MoU) on upgradation of L70 Guns for the Sri Lankan Air Force, and cooperation between National Cadet Corps and National Defence Colleges of both the countries. The upgradation of these air defence guns will strengthen the air defence architecture of critical assets in Sri Lanka. The MoU on academic cooperation will facilitate knowledge sharing to further strengthen the academic bonds between them and formalise the NCC youth exchange programme between India and Sri Lanka.Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who is on visit to Sri Lanka, today called on President Anura Kumara Dissanayake in Colombo and discussed the entire spectrum of the multi-faceted partnership between India and Sri Lanka. During the meeting, both sides reaffirmed that India and Sri Lanka will keep working jointly to ensure the safety, security, peace and prosperity of the region. President Dissanayake reiterated that Sri Lanka would never allow its territory to be used for any activities inimical to India’s security interests. Both sides also reaffirmed that as civilisational twins, close neighbours and maritime partners, they would continue to work together for their development and welfare of the people.. Meanwhile, Both leaders virtually inaugurated three Bailey Bridges constructed by the Indian Defence Forces.During the meeting, Mr Singh conveyed Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s warm greetings to Dissanayake. In return Mr Dissanayake also expressed gratitude for the relief assistance provided by India as part of Operation Sagar Bandhu during Cyclone Ditwah and the comprehensive rehabilitation package extended by New Delhi to facilitate reconstruction and rehabilitation work across different parts of the island.Mr Singh also underlined that the citizens of the two countries share deep friendship based on strong historical and civilisational links and people-to-people exchanges. Mr Singh emphasised that as a closest friend and neighbour of Sri Lanka, India considers it a responsibility to provide assistance as the first responder and would continue to do so in the future.Mr Singh also met Sri Lankan Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya and exchanged views on issues related to development cooperation, education and the close cultural and civilisational ties between India and Sri Lanka. They underlined that as sister democracies with shared heritage, India and Sri Lanka should continue to work on a shared developmental vision for the peace and prosperity of the region.

. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey stressed the need to promote Fintech innovation while ensuring investor protection and market integrity. He was speaking as he welcomed members of the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) Fintech Task Force for its plenary meeting in Mumbai today being held on the sidelines of the Global Fintech Festival 2026. He also commended the task force for the substantial progress made through its work. The IOSCO Fintech Task Force brings together securities regulators to examine developments and regulatory challenges arising from financial technologies. The plenary is being held in Mumbai during the Global Fintech Festival, which is taking place from September 8 to 11.

. The Unique Identification Authority of India, UIDAI, has launched a new Face Authentication Software Development Kit to simplify Aadhaar authentication for partner institutions and address geofencing restrictions affecting Indians travelling or living overseas.Speaking at the Global Fintech Fest 2026 in Mumbai, UIDAI Chairman Neelkanth Mishra said the new SDK will enable partner banks and businesses to run Aadhaar authentication locally on their own servers instead of routing requests through UIDAI’s central systems.Mr. Mishra said Aadhaar authentication volumes have risen from around seven crore transactions a day a few years ago to nearly ten crore currently. He said UIDAI is preparing its infrastructure to handle 25 to 30 crore authentications daily.He added that more than 600 entities currently use the Aadhaar platform, while the Aadhaar app is nearing six crore downloads..

. In Tennis, India’s Karan Singh clinched the Men’s Singles title at the ITF Men’s World Tour M15,  at Bali in Indonesia. This is Karan’s fourth career title and his third of the 2026 season — second in singles.  The fourth-seeded Indian who hails from Karnal in Haryana defeated the fifth seed Isaac Becroft of New Zealand in a closely contested final on hard courts, clinching a 7-5, 7-6 (3) win to lift the title.The singles victory in Indonesia marks a highly successful continuation of Karan’s 2026 calendar, coming just weeks after he clinched the doubles title at the ITF M15 Astana in Kazakhstan.The 23-year-old Karan has won one ATP Challenger doubles title at the 2024 Brazzaville Challenger with Florent Bax.

. India bagged five medals including two gold, two silver and one bronze on the penultimate day of the Stage three of World Archery Para Series in Ahmedabad today, with the men’s teams winning the top honours.Reigning world champion Toman Kumar and Shyam Sundar Swami clinched the gold medal in the Men’s compound team event with a dominant win over Iraq’s Abbas Kadhim and Anwer Aldawod, 152-139.Men’s duo of double Paralympic medallist Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi overcame Slovakia’s David Ivan and Denis Ivan 6-2 to bag the yellow metal in recurve team title.The women’s recurve team of Bhawna and Pooja settled for silver after going down 0-6 to Chinese pair in the final. Swati and Adil Mohamed Nazir Ansari finished runners-up in the Mixed Team W1 (recurve/compound) event, taking Silver. Swati then claimed bronze in the individual W1 category, defeating Russia’s Elena Krutova, 6-2.However, India missed out on a bronze in the women’s compound team event, with Sheetal Devi and Payal Nag losing their third-place playoff to China’s Wang Huiting and Gao Fangxia.

. The Department of Telecommunications has helped prevent suspected cyber fraud losses of more than five thousand crore rupees through its Financial Fraud Risk Indicator (FRI) within fifteen months of its launch. FRI is a multi-dimensional analytical framework launched on 22nd of May last year under its Digital Intelligence Platform to provide financial institutions with actionable, real-time intelligence for cyber fraud prevention.The Ministry of Communications has said that the milestone marks a decisive scaling-up of an initiative that had prevented 660 crore rupees of losses in its first six months of operation. It reflects the growing role of telecom intelligence in shielding citizens from digital financial fraud, and the strength of coordinated action across the telecom, banking, fintech, securities, insurance and law enforcement ecosystems.The FRI is an innovative risk-assessment framework developed by DoT to help financial institutions assess in real time, the likelihood that a mobile number may be associated with cyber-crime or financial fraud.

. The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has conducted six major operations across the country in the last 10 days, seizing two leopard skins, 180 live Indian Star Tortoises, 12 live Tokay Geckos, around 24 kilograms of Pangolin scales, and about 500 grams of Tiger bones. The Ministry of Finance reported that thirteen persons have been arrested in connection with these operations. According to the DRI, these diverse recoveries highlight the various forms of protected wildlife trafficking and underscore the need for sustained inter-agency coordination.

. In football, India qualified for the AFC U20 Asian Cup main tournament for the first time in 20 years, after a 3-nil win over Bangladesh in their final qualifying match in Tashkent yesterday.In their final Group B qualifier, Danny Meitei Laishram opened the scoring in the 25th minute, before Vishal Yadav doubled India’s lead with an acrobatic finish on the hour mark. Substitute Md Arbash made it 3-nil in the 79th minute.The victory, India’s second in the qualifiers, took them to six points from three matches. India then waited for the result of the Syria-Uzbekistan match.Uzbekistan’s 3-nil win over Syria confirmed India’s qualification as one of the seven best runners-up across the eight groups. India last featured in the AFC U20 Asian Cup in 2006. Uzbekistan topped Group B with nine points, while Syria finished third with three points. Bangladesh, who lost all three matches, were relegated to the Development Phase.The AFC U20 Asian Cup will be held in China from 24th March to 10th April, next year.

. An 8th Indian Air Force aircraft carrying 35 tonnes of relief and rescue supplies has departed for Kathmandu, Nepal. In a social media post, External Affairs Ministry said that the assistance includes NDRF equipment, rescue gear, forensic supplies and Army team replenishment supplies. It said, India is continuing its relief and rescue efforts.

. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla today paid tribute to Param Vir Chakra awardee Company Quartermaster Havildar Abdul Hamid on his martyrdom day. In a social media post, Mr Birla said that Abdul Hamid displayed indomitable courage and exceptional combat skills during the 1965 India-Pakistan War and made the supreme sacrifice for the nation.Mr Birla said that with his courage and presence of mind, Abdul Hamid destroyed several enemy tanks and remained steadfast on the frontline despite adverse conditions. Mr Birla said that by making the supreme sacrifice on the battlefield, Company Quartermaster Havildar Abdul Hamid further enriched the glorious tradition of the Indian Army. The Lok Sabha Speaker said the nation will always remember his valour and sacrifice.

. Vultures are extremely important for our ecosystem. By feeding on dead animals, they help keep the environment clean and reduce the spread of harmful diseases.However, vulture populations have declined significantly because of habitat loss, poisoning, and certain veterinary medicines that are harmful to them. Conservation efforts are therefore essential to protect these birds and maintain the balance of nature.On this International Vulture Day, government and environmental experts have urged people to understand, protect, and conserve vultures for a healthier environment.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh met Sri Lankan Prime Minister Dr Harini Amarasuriya in Colombo yesterday. The two leaders discussed several issues, with the main focus of meeting being cooperation in the field of development.They reviewed progress in areas of mutual interest, including education, information technology, infrastructure, innovation and research. They also discussed the ancient civilisational ties between India and Sri Lanka and highlighted strong people-to-people exchanges as an enduring bond between the two countries.The Defence Minister said that as sister democracies with a shared heritage, India and Sri Lanka should continue to work towards a common developmental vision for peace and prosperity in the region and the welfare of their people. He stressed that capacity building is an important pillar of bilateral cooperation.The Defence Minister also described Dr Harini Amarasuriya as a role model for women in both Sri Lanka and India and a symbol of women empowerment and Nari Shakti. He said that India would like to encourage more women from Sri Lanka to avail themselves of scholarships from the Indian Council for Cultural Relations and other Government of India initiatives aimed at increasing women’s participation in governance and leadership.

. The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has referred Iran to UN Security Council for the first time in 20 years, citing Tehran’s failure to cooperate with a long-running probe into uranium traces found at undeclared sites.The IAEA’s 35-member board approved the resolution by 23 votes to five, with eight abstentions. Russia, China, and Niger voted against it. The resolution was proposed by the United States, Britain, France, and Germany. Referring Iran to the Security Council opens the country to possible sanctions and asset freezes. However, such punitive measures are unlikely because Iran’s allies, Russia and China, are permanent Security Council members and can veto any punitive action.The IAEA said Iran has around 441 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60 percent purity, close to weapons-grade levels. The agency has also been unable to verify the status of the stockpile or access several nuclear sites following Israeli and US strikes in June last year.

. In Balochistan, two more people have been subjected to enforced disappearance by Pakistani forces, highlighting continued concerns over disappearances of Baloch people and the lack of information available to affected families. According to The Balochistan Post, Ali Baloch was allegedly detained by Pakistani forces in Mastung at around 3 am on August 23. His whereabouts remain unknown. In a separate case, the family of Shakeel Baloch said, he was taken from his residence in Killi Goharabad in Quetta at approximately midnight on April 16.The family alleged that personnel associated with Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) were involved in his disappearance. Neither family has received information regarding the two men’s whereabouts or current condition. Their continued absence has added to concerns raised by relatives and local rights activists over the pattern of alleged enforced disappearances across the province.Earlier, UN human rights experts had expressed grave concern over the alleged enforced disappearance and extra-judicial killing of Baloch resident Imran Ali in Balochistan province. The UN experts have also raised concerns over reports of other unidentified bodies and warned of a wider pattern of enforced disappearances, torture and unlawful killings in Balochistan.

. The Indian contingent for the Asian Games 2026  received a grand send-off in New Delhi yesterday in the presence of Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya. Dr. Mandaviya, along with Indian Olympic Association President P T Usha, Sports Secretary Hari Ranjan Rao, and Chef de Mission Sahdev Yadav, unveiled the official jersey of the Indian contingent in the presence of athletes and support staff.Addressing the gathering, Dr. Mandaviya urged Indian athletes to turn pressure into performance, view opponents as opportunities and transform those opportunities into achievements. Highlighting Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision for Indian sports, he said the Government has created new pathways for athletes to compete and excel at the global level.Dr Mandaviya also highlighted the growing depth of Indian sport and the emergence of young talent. He said that out of the 503-member contingent, more than three hundred athletes are first-time participants at the Asian Games. Applauding India’s performance at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow, the Union Minister said at the last Commonwealth Games, India won 13 gold medals and this time the tally has improved by more than 35 per cent. He said the target is to establish India firmly on the world sporting stage by 2036, when the country aims to host the Olympic Games. He added that this ten-year plan includes an allocation of more than 36 thousand crore rupees for improving sports infrastructure.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports informed us that the Asian Games 2026 will be held in Japan, where the Indian contingent will compete across multiple sporting disciplines. The 503-member contingent includes athletes and support staff, with more than three hundred athletes set to make their debut at the Asian Games, reflecting the growing depth and bench strength of Indian sport.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was 0.3 per cent up at 1,53,486 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, Silver rose 0.6 per cent to 2,35,249 rupees per kilogram.

. On the eve of Raksha Bandhan, President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to people. The President said that the festival of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of country’s culture and tradition since ancient times. She said that rakhi thread, tied around the wrist with faith, is regarded as a sacred bond of protection, known as Raksha Bandhan.The President  said that in many shlokas and mantras, Rakshe, Ma Chala, Ma Chala can be found which expresses the imploration that may this bond of protection continue forever. President Murmu urged every citizen to take a pledge to strengthen the bonds amongst families and communities, marching forward with this spirit towards a Viksit Bharat.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to countrymen on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said festival that celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolizes of India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall, with isolated extremely heavy rainfall, over Odisha for today.The Weather Agency has forecast heavy rainfall over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Gangetic West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Kerala, Mahe and Uttarakhand during the next two days.The Met Department has forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim till the 15th of this month. Similar conditions are likely to prevail over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Arunachal Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh till tomorrow. Hot and humid weather over Coastal Andhra Pradesh is likely today.

. Global crude oil prices surged today as escalating conflict in West Asia heightened concerns over disruptions to oil flows. Brent crude was trading 2.9 per cent up at 100 US dollars and 81 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 2.7 per cent up at 95 US dollars and 55 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal has called on BRICS countries to work together to expand opportunities for women entrepreneurs and women-led enterprises in international trade. Addressing the BRICS WBA Women-Led Development Conference in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Goyal stressed the need for easier access to credit and markets, along with predictable business rules.The Commerce Minister said India is focused on empowering women through financial inclusion, education, skills and improved quality of life, with the aim of making them drivers of the country’s growth. He noted that nearly 300 million women in India have bank accounts, while collateral-free loans are provided to women seeking to start their own work, including those without a credit history.Mr Goyal also said around 100 million rural women are members of over nine million self-help groups under the ‘Lakhpati Didis’ initiative, aimed at ensuring women’s economic independence and greater contribution to India’s growth.Mr Goyal also urged governments to encourage women-owned enterprises to participate more actively in international expositions, conferences, seminars, exhibitions and business forums. Calling for greater engagement among BRICS countries, the minister said dialogue and diplomacy are the way forward towards a more prosperous future for member countries, partner countries and the world. He also highlighted that India has set a target of growing from a four trillion dollar economy today to a thirty trillion dollar economy by 2047, when the country celebrates 100 years of Independence.

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today met former Sri Lankan cricketers Aravinda De Silva, Sanath Jayasuriya and Chaminda Vaas in Colombo. In a social media post, Mr Rajnath Singh said that these cricketers have been admired by millions in India for their exceptional performances. The Defence Minister is on a two-day visit to Sri Lanka.

. Reigning Paralympics champion Harvinder Singh and world No. 1 Sheetal Devi led the charge as India signed off their World Archery Para Series Stage III campaign in Ahmedabad on a high, winning two gold and four bronze medals, on the final day today. World No. 1 and reigning world champion Sheetal Devi held her nerve in a dramatic shoot-off to win the para compound women’s individual gold, while double Paralympics medallist Harvinder, paired with Bhawna, to clinch gold medal in the para recurve mixed team event. In the recurve mixed team final, double Paralympics medalist Harvinder and Bhawna made short work of China’s Liang Qiurong and Xia Lei, winning 6-nil in straight sets. Bhawna then added another bronze in an all-Indian para recurve women’s bronze-medal play-off, defeating compatriot Rajshree Rathod 6-nil.Sheetal returned in the evening session and produced a composed performance against Kazakhstan’s Aizada Seidan in a thrilling compound women’s individual final. Sheetal, thus, completed a medal double, having earlier teamed up with Toman Kumar to win bronze in the compound mixed team event. India also picked up a bronze in the para compound women’s individual event, with Sarita edging out China’s Wang Huiting. The campaign ended with another bronze for Toman, as the world No. 1 and reigning world champion defeated Iraq’s Abbas Kadhim in the para compound men’s individual event for his second medal of the competition.

. In US Open Tennis, Defending women’s singles champion and top seed Aryna Sabalenka has advanced to the semifinals after overcoming sixth seed Linda Nosková of the Czech Republic in a thrilling quarterfinal. Sabalenka prevailed 7-6, 3-6, 7-6 in a tightly contested match last night.In the men’s singles, 11th seed Frances Tiafoe booked his place in the last four after defeating fellow American Alex Michelsen in a five-set thriller. Tiafoe won 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6 in an all-American quarterfinal.In other women’s singles quarterfinals, third seed Jessica Pegula will take on 26th seed Emma Navarro in another all-American clash this morning, while fourth seed Coco Gauff will face fifth seed Mirra Andreeva of Russia today. Second seed Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan will be up against China’s Qinwen Zheng in the other quarterfinal. In the men’s singles, defending champion Carlos Alcaraz of Spain will take on eighth-seeded American Ben Shelton this morning.

. The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek has concluded with 13 key outcomes. The outcomes cover counter-terrorism, climate action, energy, disaster management and digital cooperation.The summit adopted the historic Bishkek Declaration, marking the SCO’s 25th anniversary. It also approved four MoUs and more than 20 decisions.A major decision was to include English as an official SCO language. Leaders also agreed to establish a Universal Centre for Countering Security Threats.The measures will strengthen cooperation against terrorism, extremism, organised crime and other transnational threats. They will also improve security information sharing.Several decisions focus on tackling drug trafficking and synthetic drugs. These include stronger coordination among law enforcement agencies and a cooperation programme on combating drug addiction until 2030. The measures support India’s efforts against cross-border narcotics trafficking and narco-terrorism.On climate and energy, SCO members agreed to enhance cooperation on energy conservation and efficiency. They also adopted a memorandum on combating climate change. These measures support India’s energy security and climate-resilient development goals.The summit also adopted a statement on assistance to countries affected by emergencies. It will strengthen cooperation in disaster management and humanitarian assistance, an area where India has significant capabilities.In the digital sector, members agreed to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence. The move will provide India an opportunity to share its digital and AI expertise and promote responsible and inclusive use of the technology.An agreement on information cooperation will also promote institutional exchanges and help strengthen India’s engagement with the regional media space.The Ministry of External Affairs said the outcomes give India a strategic platform to advance its positions on regional security, development and connectivity. They also strengthen India’s engagement with Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.The MEA said, addressing the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a roadmap for the next 25 years. He stressed the need for concrete outcomes in the areas of security, connectivity and opportunity.The two-day SCO Summit was held at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, from August 31 to September 1.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended lower for the third consecutive session today. The Sensex plunged 813 points or 1.1 per cent to close at 74,764. The Nifty also shed 204 points or 0.9 per cent to settle at 23,432.In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 and the Smallcap 100 indices also declined half a per cent each.In the Sensex pack, 24 out of 30 companies registered losses. Among the top laggards, HCL Tech lost four and a half per cent, Infosys declined 4.4 per cent, and Tech Mahindra dropped 3.9 per cent. In contrast, Adani Ports surged 3.7 per cent, Tata Steel gained 2.4 per cent and Trent rose 1.1 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 20 out of 28 sectors edged downward. Among the top underperformers, IT fell 3.2 per cent, Focused IT dropped three per cent and Realty lost two per cent. In contrast, Metal advanced 1.9 per cent, Hospitals gained 1.4 per cent and Utilities added 1.1 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2600 companies declined, 1792 advanced and 196 remained unchanged.

. The National Consumer Helpline (NCH) has facilitated refunds of more than 105 crore rupees to consumers across 35 sectors by addressing over one lakh 66 thousand refund-related grievances. These grievances were from the fifteen-month period from 25th April 2025 to 31st July 2026. The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution said that the refunds were facilitated at the pre-litigation stage, enabling consumers to obtain timely relief without having to approach the Consumer Commissions. The Ministry noted that the e-commerce sector accounted for the largest share of refund-related grievances, with over one lakh complaints resulting in refunds of more than 74 crore rupees. The Travel and Tourism sector followed, with refunds exceeding 10 crore rupees.The Ministry highlighted that NCH operates through a convergence-based mechanism under which consumer grievances are digitally forwarded to the concerned companies for resolution within defined timelines. It added that refund-related grievances received through NCH have come from metropolitan cities as well as remote regions across the country, reflecting the platform’s reach as a pan-India mechanism for consumer grievance redressal. The Ministry noted that the National Consumer Helpline provides consumers access to grievance redressal in 17 languages through multiple channels. It also encouraged the consumers to proactively utilise the National Consumer Helpline to safeguard their consumer rights and seek redressal of their grievances.

. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan has said that the country today stands as an important place of transformation and renewed confidence, showcasing the results of collective determination and efforts. The Vice President said this after releasing a book titled Sankalp Se Siddhi ka Modi Yug written by Rajya Sabha MP Ghanshyam Tiwari. He said that whether it is advancing technology, building modern infrastructure, and strengthening national unity and promoting women-led development, education is the tool for empowerment. Mr Radhakrishnan also highlighted the contributions of the country’s youth, women, farmers, workers, and every citizen for their involvement in building a stronger and prosperous nation. He also underlined that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is the only leader in the world to provide free Covid-19 vaccines not only to 140 crore Indian people but also to hundred more countries.Speaking about the book, the Vice President said that through the publication, the author seeks to bring together many aspects of country’s larger narratives, reviving pride in cultural heritage and enhancing the country’s voice at the global stage. He added that the book reflects the journey of the nation and encourages everyone and boosts their enthusiasm.

. India has intensified its humanitarian assistance to Nepal in the wake of devastating flash floods, delivering over 130 tonnes of relief material and deploying 54 expert personnel to support search, rescue, and forensic operations. The Indian Embassy in Nepal said yesterday that an eighth Indian Air Force aircraft carrying 35 tonnes of relief and rescue supplies landed in Kathmandu, marking the latest shipment in a continuous aid effort launched on August 26, 2026.India has also dispatched specialised technical gear, including mud rescue suits, gas detectors, breathing apparatus, inflatable walkways, portable generators, lighting towers, and dewatering pumps. India has provided DNA kits, reagents, and equipment for DNA profiling to aid in victim identification.Earlier, the Ministry of External Affairs also noted the handing over of the relief aid by Indian Ambassador Naveen Srivastava to Nepal’s Minister Mahabir Pun upon the arrival of the eighth aircraft.Meanwhile, India’s specialised tunnel rescue team initially launched joint operations with the Nepali Army across two high-risk sites in Chilime and Langtang. Search efforts are currently concentrated at the Chilime tunnel, where rescue workers face severe operational hurdles due to rugged terrain, constrained access, and steep tunnel inclines. Teams are currently constructing a makeshift access path to transport heavy machinery, such as excavators, directly to the tunnel entrance. Construction on the track is progressing steadily and is expected to be completed within two to three days.

. The Government is preparing to introduce a new and stringent Seed Act aimed at protecting the country’s farmers from the losses caused by fake and substandard seeds. Union Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will hold a high-level consultation with senior leaders of major farmer organisations from across the country in New Delhi, tomorrow, in this regard. The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare said that the proposed legislation is part of the government’s efforts to realise Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of a prosperous and self-reliant farming community. It added that the consultation is aimed at incorporating farmers’ ground-level experiences, suggestions and concerns directly into the draft seed legislation. The Ministry further said that the proposed new Seed Act is expected to provide for stringent legal action against companies and traders involved in the sale of fake, adulterated or substandard seeds, including heavy penalties and imprisonment. The government intends to build a robust and effective regulatory framework to curb the activities of seed mafias and protect farmers from fraudulent and poor-quality seeds.The consultation will bring farmer representatives together from Bharatiya Kisan Sangh, various factions of the Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU), All India Kisan Coordination Committee (AIKCC), Kisan Mahapanchayat, Bharatiya Krishak Samaj, Gaon Kisan Unnayan and the Society for Independent Farmers Association (SIFA). Ground-level farmer representatives from several states will also put forward their views before the Union Agriculture Minister.

. In the US Open, American Ben Shelton stormed into the men’s singles semifinals. Shelton beat defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set thriller, 6-7, 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6, in the quarterfinals at Arthur Ashe Stadium today. Shelton will now face compatriot Frances Tiafoe in the semi-finals. Both Americans will be chasing a maiden Grand Slam final appearance.For Alcaraz, the defeat ended his bid for an eighth Grand Slam title and a chance to become the first man since Roger Federer to successfully defend the US Open crown.

. The government has cleared eight railway multitracking projects involving an investment of over 20 thousand 800 crore rupees. The projects are aimed at increasing line capacity, improving operational efficiency and easing congestion on key routes.Briefing the media after the Cabinet meeting yesterday, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said, three projects, costing over 10 thousand 783 crore rupees, will cover 14 districts across West Bengal, Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, adding about 656 kilometres to the existing railway network. These include the Kharagpur-Jharsuguda fourth line, Katni-Pendra Road fourth line and Bilaspur-Pendra Road third line. They are planned for completion by 2029-30.The other five projects, at the cost of nearly 10 thousand 21 crore rupees, will cover 17 districts in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana, adding about 540 kilometres to the network. These include the Arakkonam-Renigunta third and fourth lines, Whitefield-Bangarapet third and fourth lines, and doubling of the Hosur-Omalur line. The projects will enhance connectivity to around two thousand one hundred villages with a population of about 52 lakh.Mr Vaishnaw also said the government has decided to quadruple all seven high-density railway corridors, covering around 11 thousand kilometres. These include Delhi-Howrah, Mumbai-Howrah, Delhi-Mumbai, Delhi-Guwahati, Delhi-Chennai, Howrah-Chennai and Mumbai-Chennai.Four-lining of 2,000 kilometres has already been completed.On the Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train Project, Mr Vaishnaw said the service will commence next year. He said construction is progressing rapidly and the initial 100-kilometre section from Surat to Vapi will be opened.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said the Cabinet decisions on the railway multitracking projects will ensure faster passenger movement, stronger connectivity and additional freight capacity. He said the projects will strengthen rail connectivity in South India and benefit lakhs of people.The Prime Minister also said the multitracking projects will expand the railway network and improve connectivity across Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal. He said the projects will also promote tourism, particularly heritage and wildlife tourism, and help reduce logistics costs.

. The Financial Action Task Force, FATF, has warned countries about the growing misuse of gaming and gambling platforms for financial crimes.FATF said criminals are using gambling platforms to move money without actually gambling, splitting large amounts into multiple small transactions and placing unusual or coordinated bets to avoid detection. It has also flagged illegal and unlicensed online gambling as a major risk. Criminals may use multiple payment methods, fake identities and complex ownership structures to conceal their activities.The new FATF risk indicators are aimed at helping governments, regulators and businesses detect suspicious transactions and tackle money laundering, terrorist financing and other financial crimes linked to the gaming and gambling sectors.

. The Government has announced the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards for the year 2024. The awards recognise outstanding achievements by individuals in the field of adventure and seek to promote a spirit of endurance, risk-taking, teamwork and quick and effective decision-making in challenging situations. The awards are given in four categories, which are Land Adventure, Water Adventure, Air Adventure and Lifetime Achievement. Each awardee will receive a statuette, a certificate and award money of 15 lakh rupees. The awardees are Baljeet Kaur and Skalzang Rigzin in Land Adventure category, Rimo Saha in Water Adventure category and Shiv Prasad Chamoli in the Life Time Achievement category.The selections were made following the recommendations of the National Selection Committee. The Committee evaluated the nominations and recommended the awardees for conferment of the national honour.The awards seek to promote among the youth a spirit of courage, endurance, discipline, risk-taking and cooperative teamwork, while encouraging the ability to respond with speed and effectiveness in challenging situations. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the awards along with the National Sports Awards 2025. The date of the award ceremony will be announced later.

. Ahead of the BRICS Leaders’ Summit, the final BRICS Finance Ministers’ and Central Bank Governors’ meeting is taking place in Mumbai on September 9-10. This year’s BRICS Finance Track is guided by the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”.Previously, the Finance Ministers and Governors had met in Jaipur last month. Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Nirmala Sitharaman reviewed key outcomes of the BRICS Finance Track before the scheduled final meeting in Mumbai.
. In the forex market, the rupee depreciated by 28 paise to close at 95.11 rupees against the US dollar.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will share his thoughts with the people of the country and abroad in the Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani at 11 AM on Sunday. It will be the 137th episode of the monthly radio programme. The programme will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani and Doordarshan network, the AIR News website, and the Newsonair mobile app. It will also be live-streamed on the YouTube channels of AIR News, DD News, the PMO, and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Akashvani will broadcast the programme in regional languages immediately after the Hindi broadcast.

. India has endorsed the Call to Action for 6G Leadership and Security, joining a group of like-minded governments that have committed to shaping the sixth generation of wireless communications on the principles of openness, interoperability, security, resilience, resource efficiency and innovation-led competition. Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia announced this in a social media post. Mr Scindia said that the global partnership will help accelerate the development of secure 6G wireless networks and coordinate national strategies well ahead of 6G’s expected rollout in the 2030s. The Minister said the initiative complements India’s ongoing work in global standardisation and spectrum fora, as the nation strives to secure 10 percent of global 6G standards.Under the Call to Action, participating governments affirm that secure digital infrastructure is essential to technological competitiveness, economic prosperity and national security, and that advanced telecommunications networks are both the gateway to and the heart of that infrastructure. The initiative also reaffirms that shaping the future of 6G calls for concerted action in collaboration with industry, academia and other stakeholders.The Department of Telecommunications will take forward India’s engagement under the Call to Action and coordinate the relevant follow-up activities with concerned government agencies, industry, academia and other stakeholders. The endorsement was announced on the sidelines of the G20 Innovation Ministerial, held in North Carolina, United States this month.

. India has condemned the reported Houthi attacks on Saudi sovereign territory, especially the targeting of civilian and economic facilities. In response to a media query on the attacks in Saudi Arabia, External Affairs Ministry Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that such attacks that undermine regional security and stability and threaten freedom of navigation in the Bab-el-Mandeb were unacceptable.

. The Indian men’s junior hockey team has entered the semi-finals of the Junior Hockey Asia Cup in Moqi, China. The five-time champions thrashed Chinese Taipei 15-nil today to seal the top spot in Pool A. India finished with 10 points from three wins and a draw. Captain Anmol Ekka was the star of the match, scoring six goals. He found the net in the 25th, 29th, 32nd, 33rd, 45th and 51st minutes, all from penalty corners. Aryan Zes scored a hat-trick, while Harpal struck twice. Prabhdeep Singh, Gurusewak Singh, Arjun Santosh Hargude and Ajit Yadav scored one goal each.Meanwhile, the Indian junior women’s hockey team has reached the quarter-finals after playing out a goalless draw against China in their final Elite Pool match. India will face arch-rivals Pakistan in the quarter-final on Thursday.

. The government has extended the last date for submission of applications by selected meritorious students for National Means cum Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) for 2026-27 to 30th September this year. The NMMSS is implemented through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP). Following the extension, the last date for Level-1 verification at the Institute Nodal Officer is 15th October while the last date for Level-2 verification with the District Nodal Officer is 31st October.The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to prevent drop-out of students after elementary level that is Class eight and encourage them to complete their school education up to higher secondary level that is Class 12. The scholarship amount is 12 thousand rupees per annum per student.The Scheme provides one lakh fresh scholarships every year for Class 9 students who clear the qualifying exam for the scholarship conducted by the State and UT governments. The scholarship is continued through renewal mode from Classes 10 to 12 based on the student’s academic performance. The scheme is applicable only to students studying in State Government, Government-aided and local body schools.The eligibility parameters for availing the scholarship include parental income of not more than 3.50 lakh rupees per annum, a minimum of 55 per cent marks or equivalent grade in the Class 8 examination for appearing in the selection test for award of scholarship. The government has advised all the eligible students to complete their scholarship applications on the National Scholarship Portal within the extended timeline.
